title: install_e2e's cp -a of a live checkout can tear, and the append-only guard then refuses the fixture commit
body:
install_e2e.bats:27 builds its fixture with `cp -a "$UTILZ_HOME" "$src"`, copying the whole live checkout INCLUDING .git. The copy is not atomic: cp walks the tree over seconds, and on this project three whiteboard nodes (cc, vc, devbin-vc) write and commit continuously. When a peer commits DURING the walk, the fixture ends up with a .git and a worktree from different instants.

OBSERVED 2026-09-20, the shell leg of `devbin test all` (bats 602 of 612 expected, setup_file failed at install_e2e.bats:48):

  fixture_commit: the commit "e2e fixture" ... was refused:
  error: append-only path(s) lost lines in this commit -- refusing.
    intent/.canon/events/2026/09/20/01M2ZFA1NTSF0XY92ZB8KZEQ7C.json -- 15 line(s) removed, 0 added
    (and two more)

MECHANISM, confirmed rather than inferred. Those three event files were written at 14:15:24-14:16:24 local, inside the run's window (14:10:57-14:23:17). cc's localfold 0ffe1dd committed them, moving HEAD off 633a1a1 mid-run. The fixture's .git was copied AFTER that commit, so the fixture's HEAD carries the three files at 15 lines each; its worktree was copied BEFORE they existed, so it lacks them. `git add -A` then stages three deletions, and the append-only guard correctly refuses what looks like a write landing where an append was meant.

WHY IT MATTERS: the failure is maximally misleading. It reads as data loss in the append-only event store, which is alarming and wrong, and it names files the developer never touched. The suite's own comment at install_e2e.bats:52 records 'a flaky failure here undiagnosable on 8 Sep' -- plausibly this.

CI never sees it: no concurrent writer there. Run 35512936209 on the same commit was green on all seven jobs while this went red locally.

THE FIX, and it is one line of ordering. The guard refuses REMOVALS and permits ADDITIONS. So copy .git FIRST and the worktree SECOND: any tear then leaves the worktree NEWER than HEAD, which stages as additions and passes. Today's order makes the worktree older than HEAD, which stages as deletions and fails. Alternatives considered: a git clone would be consistent but loses the mtimes that keep cargo's fingerprints valid, which is why cp -a was chosen (install_e2e.bats:25). Excluding intent/ from the copy does NOT work, although the publish never reads it (install.sh:99 enumerates only bin, opt, help, static and VERSION): the fixture keeps .git, so a worktree without intent/ makes `git add -A` stage the deletion of every tracked intent/ file, events included, and the guard would refuse the fixture commit on every run rather than on some. (Corrected 2026-09-21; the first filing listed it as working.)
